transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been doing some odd things at church. Like, I’ll stand by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up and just not move, or I’ll fold the same stack of napkins over and over while people are waiting on me. It’s embarrassing, and I don’t really know why I’m doing it.

When you're standing there holding the spoon or folding the napkins over and over, does it feel like you're doing it on purpose to relieve some anxious feeling, or does it feel more like your body just gets stuck and you can't help it?

It feels more like I just get stuck. I’m not really doing it to calm myself down or anything. I’ll be there with the spoon up, or folding those same napkins again and again, and people are waiting… and I know it looks odd, but I don’t seem to stop right away.
Have you noticed anything else unusual lately, like hearing voices or sounds other people don't hear, or having beliefs that others don't share or find strange?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed hearing voices or sounds other folks don’t hear. And I can’t think of any beliefs like that… it’s more just the getting stuck with things.
During these episodes, if someone tries to gently move your arm or guide you to put the spoon down, what happens—do you resist, stay stiff, or go along with it?

I’m not really sure about that part. What I notice is I’m just standing there with the serving spoon held up, not moving, or I’ll keep folding the same napkins while folks are waiting. I don’t mean to make trouble… I just seem to get stuck doing it.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, new medications, or substance use around the time these episodes started?

I don’t really know. I can’t think of any sickness or a fall or anything like that around when it started. I’m not sure about medicines—nothing comes to mind. And I don’t use drugs or anything like that.
Over the past several months, have you noticed yourself becoming more withdrawn, showing less emotion, or losing interest in things you used to care about, even outside of these stuck episodes?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed that I’m more withdrawn or anything. I still feel about the same, I think. Nothing stands out to me like losing interest, no.
Have you had any recent blood tests, brain scans, or other medical work-ups done, and if so, did any of them show anything abnormal?
I don’t think I’ve had anything like that done recently. If I did, nobody told me anything was abnormal. I’m not really sure.

Has anyone in your family ever been diagnosed with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or another serious mental illness, or have you yourself had any past episodes of unusual thinking, hearing things, or strange beliefs before this?
I don’t really know of anyone in my family having something like that. Nobody ever told me about that. And for me, before this, I can’t think of any past times like that, not that I remember.
During these episodes, have you or anyone around you noticed things like a fever, sweating, a fast heartbeat, muscle stiffness, or tremors happening at the same time?
I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed a fever or shaking or anything like that. Nobody’s really told me they saw that happening either.
Do you have any diagnosed medical conditions—such as thyroid problems, epilepsy, diabetes, or other neurological issues—that a doctor has told you about?
Not that I know of. I don’t remember a doctor telling me I have thyroid trouble, seizures, diabetes, or anything with my nerves like that.
How long has this been going on—weeks, months, or longer since you first noticed yourself getting 'stuck' like this?
It’s been about six months, I think. That’s when people started noticing I was getting stuck like that and my talking wasn’t always making sense.

You mentioned your talking sometimes 'wasn't making sense' around the same time this started—can you tell me more about that? For example, do you find yourself losing track of what you're saying, or do others say your sentences don't connect logically?

Yes… I do lose the point sometimes. Like if the ladies ask me about blankets or choir practice, I mean to answer plain, but then my words go off somewhere else. I’ll start talking about beans, then hymns, then my roses, and I can tell by their faces they don’t know what I’m trying to say.
Over these past six months, have you noticed any change in your ability to take care of daily tasks, like cooking, cleaning, or keeping up with your usual responsibilities at church or home?

Yes… some. I’ve had to step back from choir things and helping at church like I used to. I mix up plans, or I get the wrong person in my head, and then folks get uneasy or someone has to fix what I was supposed to do. So I don’t take on as much now.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with prominent catatonic behaviors (motor immobility/posturing with the serving spoon, stereotyped repetitive napkin folding) that are non-goal-directed and not anxiolytic in nature, occurring alongside disorganized speech (derailment/loose associations - beans, hymns, roses) and functional decline (withdrawal from church/choir duties) over a 6-month period. Medical, substance, and neurological causes were screened and ruled out (no fever, autonomic instability, medication changes, head injury, or diagnosed medical conditions), reducing likelihood of catatonia due to a general medical condition (F06.1). No mood symptoms, hallucinations, or delusions were endorsed, and there was no prior psychiatric history, but the combination of catatonic motor symptoms as a predominant feature with disorganized speech in the context of a schizophrenia-spectrum presentation supports catatonic-type schizophrenia (F20.2) over disorganized (F20.1) or undifferentiated (F20.3) subtypes.
